knowledge_point.title: The Parametric Equations of an Ellipse Centered at a General Point

question.:question/problem: Consider the ellipse centered at $(6,-2)$ with horizontal radius $8$ and vertical radius $7.$ Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $\theta \in [0,2\pi ),$ generate the ellipse?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at the point $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\cos\theta+h,\,y=b\sin\theta+k,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

In our case, the ellipse is centered at the point $(6,-2),$ $a=8$ and $b=7.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the ellipse are

$$
x=8\cos\theta+6,\,y=7\sin\theta-2,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

Consider the ellipse centered at $(-2,-4)$ with horizontal radius $5$ and vertical radius $6.$ Construct a set of parametric equations, defined for $\theta \in [0,2\pi ),$ that traverse the ellipse once in the counterclockwise direction starting at the point $A(3,-4).$

$x=$ {{field-1}}$,\,y=$ {{field-2}}$,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at the point $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\cos\theta+h,\,y=b\sin\theta+k,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

Under this parametrization, the ellipse is traversed once in the counterclockwise direction, starting from $(h+a,k).$

In our case, the ellipse is centered at the point $(-2,-4),$ $a=5$ and $b=6.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the ellipse are

$$
x=5\cos\theta-2,\,y=6\sin\theta-4,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$
